resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO), residential
resale_co.issued_by: Township of West Orange Construction Official, with Zoning Official approval (Department of Planning & Development)
resale_co.valid_for: A temporary CCO may be issued for minor violations, with repairs due within 30 days or as set by the construction official; the permanent CCO then has no added fee
requirements: Inspection for compliance with Township and State health and safety codes, fire safety (Chapter 18, Section 3) and the Land Use Regulations
Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors installed (battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units)
Sidewalk and walkway condition, entrance steps with balusters and handrails, basement stairway
Electrical hazards, grounded receptacles, relief valves on boilers and water heaters, sump pump discharge, venting of heating equipment and bathrooms
General property maintenance and structural condition; unregistered and commercial vehicles removed
Zoning conformance for the use of the property; work possibly done without permits is noted
Electricity and water on for the inspection
CCO states the maximum number of occupants

fees.label: Determination that a CCO is not required before a sale
fees.quote: shall pay to the Township a fee of two hundred fifty ($250.00) dollars for such determination

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Residential CCO application (typed or neatly printed; mark Sale, single or multi-family; owner, buyer, inspection contact and closing date) and submit it with a check or money order payable to 'Township of West Orange'. Fees are not refunded once processed. Zoning Enforcement, Property Maintenance & Housing, 66 Main Street Room 200, West Orange, NJ 07052.

evidence.quote: Prior to the sale or rental of any existing residential structure containing one (1) unit or more, a Certificate of Continued Occupancy must be obtained which shall be issued by the Construction Official or designated agency or department provided with the authority to grant and issue such certificates.
***PLEASE NOTE: THERE ARE NO REFUNDS ONCE APPLICATION IS PROCESSED***

To the extent that an owner fails to obtain a Certificate of Continued Occupancy and closes title, the owner shall remain liable for a separate violation on each day until a Certificate of Continued Occupancy is issued.
Geniece Gary-Adams Director Planning & Development/Zoning Official Email Geniece Gary-Adams Phone: (973) 325-4119

resale_co.notes: The Residential CCO packet (scanned PDF on the Zoning Enforcement, Property Maintenance & Housing page) includes the application, Code Section 25-40.2d, a CCO conditions checklist and smoke/CO requirements. Property Maintenance Inspectors: Fatima Baez-Aguilar (973) 325-4115, Lou DePasquale (973) 325-4200, Will Ordonez (973) 325-4118; office hours 8:30 to 10:00 a.m. and 3:30 to 4:30 p.m. The packet also lists fees for three to six units ($350.00 to $575.00) and commercial space. The Tax Assessor is to tell anyone requesting a tax search that a CCO is required. A copy of the lease is required for rentals. Rental CCOs and the lead-based paint rental inspection program are rental items, not resale items.

requirements: Battery smoke detectors and combination units in 1-2 family homes must be 10-year sealed battery alarms, with the manufacture date written on the outside
Hardwired smoke detector systems may not be downgraded to battery systems
Carbon monoxide detector in or outside the bedroom area, no more than 10 feet from any bedroom; battery or plug-in units are acceptable

authorities.name: West Orange Building Department (smoke and CO detectors checked as part of the CCO); fire code LEA: West Orange Fire Department, Fire Prevention Bureau
authorities.how_to_apply: The smoke and carbon monoxide detector check is part of the Residential CCO inspection (see resale certificate). No separate smoke certificate application or fee was found on the Fire Department pages; confirm whether the Fire Prevention Bureau issues a separate certificate.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (FireOfficial@westorange.org, 973-325-4175); Construction Official is Tom Biondi, Jr.

evidence.quote: ALL BATTERY-OPERATED single station smoke detectors and combination units, (which include smoke detectors), installed in one-and two-family dwellings SHALL be ten-year sealed battery powered alarms.

The application of such permit shall be made by the owner of record and shall comply with such administrative provisions as required by the Construction Official in accordance with N.J.A.C. 52:27D-198.1.
As the "Local Enforcing Agency", the Fire Prevention Bureau and the Fire Official are responsible for the administration and enforcement of the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code.
West Orange Twp SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: West Orange Fire Dept

fire_cert.notes: The West Orange CCO ordinance ties the CCO to the state smoke detector law (cited as N.J.A.C. 52:27D-198.1, which is the statute N.J.S.A. 52:27D-198.1), and the CCO checklist includes smoke and CO detectors, so the smoke/CO check appears to be done within the CCO. The DCA directory, however, lists the West Orange Fire Department (415 Valley Rd, (973) 325-4100) as the smoke detector compliance contact, so confirm whether a separate Fire Department certificate or fee applies. The CCO packet does not mention a fire extinguisher.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: All open permits must be closed for the CCO.

other_items.label: Sidewalk and walkways
other_items.detail: Condition of sidewalks and walkways is on the CCO checklist.

other_items.label: Tax search notice
other_items.detail: The Tax Assessor advises anyone requesting a tax assessment search that a CCO is required for the sale.

open_questions: Does the West Orange Fire Prevention Bureau issue a separate smoke/CO certificate (and fee) for 1-2 family sales, or is it covered entirely by the CCO?
